descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-92579 AC 2; TFA-94700 AC 4-5; UAT TC-24 ER 4-6 · “Deleting a patient hard-deletes all of their data immediately (backups per OAT-04) and keeps the audit log.”. Mixed: stated part — patient delete asks first and removes; account delete asks once, removes everything, keeps audit; task completed/deleted separate; no delete-every-patient control; our part — colleague left untouched after account delete (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Approach · TC-24 Deletions · S04 Existing specs: patient and account delete, the trail they keep, the removal and task events, and no delete-every-patient control

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U4 Completing a task and deleting a task are separate actions, and each is logged as its own analytics event (task completed / task deleted), one per tap, against the chart. (UAT TC-24; UAT OAT-06 item 7; TFA-94514 AC 2)
  • U5 Deleting a patient hard-deletes all of that patient's data immediately (removed, not hidden), and the audit log is kept. (UAT TC-24; TFA-92579 AC 2; TFA-94699 AC 4)
  • U9 No bulk delete anywhere in the app: records are deleted one at a time, and there is no 'delete all patients' or similar control. (UAT TC-24; TFA-92579 AC 2; TFA-94700 AC 5; TFA-94699 AC 6)
  • T2 Delete account asks for confirmation once, permanently deletes the account and all of that physician's patient data (reusing the patient hard delete), keeps the audit log, and signs out. (TFA-94700 AC 4)
  • T4 Deleting a patient is logged as one 'patient removed' analytics event with the removal reason and the care setting, in both modes. (TFA-94514 AC 1; UAT OAT-06 item 2)

Test design technique: Happy path (happy-path) — Walk the normal flow exactly as the UAT / ticket words it; everything it names has to show up.

Given Tim's chromium and api fixtures: one Hospital chart; a physician with patients in every table and a colleague; a fresh signed-in account

When Run the ten tests below unchanged, matched by title

Then forms.spec: removing a patient asks first, a dismiss keeps it, an accept removes the card and rounding:list no longer returns it; Settings has Delete account and no way to delete every patient. audit.spec: a chart delete writes a PHI_WRITE row. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Playwright assertions in the named files. What they do not show: forms.spec 'asks first, and the patient survives a cancel' passes only with a native window.confirm (it listens with page.once('dialog')), so it does not support TFA-92579 AC 7 and must change when AC 7 ships; 'confirming removal…' checks rounding:list only, not a hard delete (S03 reads the tables). …

Where it ran: local lane A (existing Playwright tests); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)

S04 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-24.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane A.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: API · API (Convex functions) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: matrix (lane A).

UAT item: TC-24 Deletions · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: TC-24/S04
